chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
It is disliked that a nail be trimmed for the deceased, or that hair be cut for him, or that his pubic hair be shaved, or that one of his joints be pressed.

key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: it is considered disliked in legal ruling

ai.seo_question: What actions are disliked to perform on the body of the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the treatment of the deceased before burial preparations are completed. It states that trimming nails, cutting hair, shaving the pubic area, and pressing the joints of the dead person are all disliked acts.
